content_sections.heading: Department-wise Vacancies
content_sections.text: The number of vacancies is tentative. The University reserves the right to increase or decrease the number of posts at the time of selection, and the number of Guest Faculty to be engaged will be decided on actual requirement.

content_sections.heading: Qualification and Experience
content_sections.text: The notice does not print an experience requirement. A Master's degree with 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale wherever the grading system is followed) in a concerned/relevant/allied subject from an Indian University, or an equivalent degree from an accredited foreign university. In addition, the candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC or the CSIR, or a similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET. Candidates who are or have been awarded a Ph.D. degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum Standards and Procedure for Award of M.Phil./Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments are exempted from NET/SLET/SET. NET/SLET/SET is also not required for Master's programmes in disciplines for which NET/SLET/SET is not conducted by the UGC, CSIR or a similar UGC-accredited test. Candidates registered for the Ph.D. programme prior to 11 July 2009 are governed by the Ordinances, Bye-laws or Regulations of the institution awarding the degree. They are exempted from NET/SLET/SET if all of these conditions are met: The fulfilment of these conditions is to be certified by the Registrar or the Dean (Academic Affairs) of the University concerned. The Ph.D. degree has been obtained from a foreign university/institution with a ranking among the top 500 in the World University Ranking (at any time) by any one of: Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), the Times Higher Education (THE), or the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) of the Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Shanghai). A relaxation of 5% marks may be provided at Graduate and Master's level for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Differently-abled (physically and visually differently-abled) and Other Backward Class (OBC) (non-creamy layer) categories, for eligibility and for assessing good academic record during engagement of temporary faculty. It applies only to qualifying marks, without any grace mark procedure. A relaxation of 5% (from 55% to 50%) may be provided to Ph.D. degree holders who obtained their Master's degree prior to 19 September 1991. A relevant grade regarded as equivalent to 55% marks, wherever a recognised university follows the grading system, is also considered eligible. The notice asks candidates to satisfy themselves beforehand that they hold the minimum essential qualification. See the official notification for the full eligibility wording.

rows.qualification: Eligibility A or B, as set out below. Specialization / relevant discipline: NET or Ph.D. in English; Master's degree in English, English Literature, Linguistics, Film Studies, English Language & Literature, Communicative English or Translation Studies.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Terms
content_sections.text: Pay: Rs. 1500/- per lecture, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,000/- per month. Payment will be made on an hourly basis as per University norms. The engagement is purely temporary, initially for one semester or as per requirement of the University. It may be extended on the basis of the University's requirement and the incumbent's satisfactory performance. The Guest Faculty will not get allowances, pension, gratuity and leave as admissible to regular teachers. The engaged candidate is not entitled to residential accommodation, official transport, leave encashment or any other allowances/facilities admissible to a regular employee. The University may modify, withdraw or cancel any communication to candidates if an inadvertent mistake in the selection process is detected at any stage, even after the engagement letter or joining.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The notice describes shortlisting followed by an interview before the Selection Committee. The marking scheme is not specified in the notice. Shortlisted candidates may be invited to appear before the Selection Committee. No TA/DA is admissible for attending the interview. The list of shortlisted candidates will be published on the official website ( www.cuj.ac.in ) under the Careers Section. The interview will be held only for shortlisted candidates on 20 November 2026 from 10:30 a.m. onwards. Reporting time is 9:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. The interview may continue the next day depending on circumstances, so candidates should come prepared accordingly. The interview date may change; any change will be notified on the University website.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required
content_sections.text: Duly filled-in application form with certificate, mark sheet and experience certificate etc. Ph.D. holders whose degree was awarded under the UGC Regulations 2009 or 2016: a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure I) from the concerned University that the Ph.D. complies with the UGC regulation. Annexure I applies to candidates registered for the Ph.D. on or after 11 July 2009. Candidates registered for the Ph.D. before 11 July 2009: a certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure II) from the concerned University/Institute. It is signed by the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice Chancellor or Dean (Academic Affairs). SC/ST/OBC candidates: a caste certificate from the competent authority in the prescribed format (Annexure III for SC/ST, Annexure IV for OBC). OBC candidates: a valid caste certificate of the current financial year in the Government of India proforma, stating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer. Candidates claiming the PH category: a medical certificate from the competent authority.

faq.question: Q1. How many Guest Faculty posts are vacant at CUJ?
faq.answer: The Central University of Jharkhand has advertised 1 post, in the UR category, in the Department of English Studies. The number is tentative and the University may increase or decrease it at the time of selection.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for CUJ Guest Faculty 2026?
faq.answer: The application must be received by email by 5:00 p.m. on 17 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for CUJ Guest Faculty in English Studies?
faq.answer: Under Eligibility A, a Master's degree with 55% marks (or equivalent grade) in a concerned, relevant or allied subject plus NET/SLET/SET, or a qualifying Ph.D. exempting NET. Under Eligibility B, a Ph.D. from a foreign university ranked in the top 500 of QS, THE or ARWU.

faq.question: Q4. What is the pay for CUJ Guest Faculty?
faq.answer: The Guest Faculty will be paid Rs. 1500/- per lecture, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,000/- per month.

faq.question: Q5. How do I apply for CUJ Guest Faculty?
faq.answer: Fill in the prescribed application form from the Career Section of www.cuj.ac.in. Email it with certificates, mark sheets and experience certificates to [email protected].

faq.question: Q6. When is the CUJ Guest Faculty interview?
faq.answer: The interview for shortlisted candidates is on 20 November 2026 from 10:30 a.m. onwards, with reporting from 9:30 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. It may continue the next day, and any change in date will be notified on the University website.

faq.question: Q7. Is the CUJ Guest Faculty job permanent?
faq.answer: No. The engagement is purely temporary, initially for one semester or as per the University's requirement. It may be extended based on the University's requirement and satisfactory performance.

faq.question: Q8. Is TA/DA paid for attending the CUJ interview?
faq.answer: No. The notice states that no TA/DA will be admissible for attending the interview.

faq.question: Q9. Is there any relaxation in marks for reserved categories?
faq.answer: Yes. A relaxation of 5% marks may be provided at Graduate and Master's level for SC, ST, differently-abled (physically and visually) and OBC (non-creamy layer) candidates. Ph.D. holders whose Master's was obtained before 19 September 1991 may get 5% relaxation, from 55% to 50%.
